title: Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 Internships | Remote Opportunities in Research and Policy Advocacy
summary: Women’s World Banking is now accepting applications for its Fall 2026 internship opportunities. Graduate students interested in international development, women’s economic empowerment, public policy, research, and financial inclusion have an exciting chance to gain practical experience with one of the world’s leading organizations dedicated to advancing women’s financial inclusion. With more than four decades of experience working alongside financial institutions, policymakers, investors, and development partners, Women’s World Banking has become a global leader in creating economic opportunities for women. The Fall 2026 internship program provides aspiring professionals with the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects while developing valuable skills and expanding their professional networks. The organization is currently recruiting graduate student interns for two key positions within the Women’s World Banking Institute. About Women’s World Banking Women’s World Banking is a global nonprofit organization focused on expanding women’s financial inclusion and economic participation. For over 40 years, the organization has worked with financial institutions worldwide to design innovative financial products and services that meet the needs of women, particularly those who have been underserved by traditional financial systems. Through research, policy advocacy, leadership development, and strategic partnerships, Women’s World Banking helps create financial ecosystems that empower women entrepreneurs, workers, and consumers. The organization’s mission is to ensure that women have access to the financial tools, services, and opportunities needed to achieve economic security and resilience. Available Internship Opportunities Women’s World Banking is currently offering the following internship positions for Fall 2026: Research Intern – Women’s World Banking Institute The Research Intern will support the Institute’s ongoing work on women’s financial inclusion through both qualitative and quantitative research activities. Responsibilities may include: * Conducting literature reviews and background research * Supporting data collection and analysis * Assisting with report preparation and research publications * Contributing to evidence-based projects on financial inclusion * Supporting research initiatives that examine barriers and opportunities for women’s economic participation This internship is ideal for graduate students with strong analytical skills and an interest in research, economics, development studies, public policy, finance, or related fields. Policy Advocacy Intern – Women’s World Banking Institute The Policy Advocacy Intern will support research and policy initiatives related to women’s financial inclusion at both national and global levels. Key responsibilities may include: * Monitoring policy developments affecting women’s financial inclusion * Conducting policy research and analysis * Supporting advocacy initiatives and policy campaigns * Assisting with stakeholder engagement activities * Preparing policy briefs and supporting materials This role is particularly suitable for students interested in public policy, international development, governance, advocacy, economics, and gender equality. Internship Benefits Interns selected for the Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 program will benefit from: * Hands-on experience in international development * Exposure to global financial inclusion initiatives * Opportunities to work on real-world projects * Professional mentorship and guidance * Practical experience in research and policy development * Collaboration with experienced professionals and global partners * Flexible and remote working opportunities * Networking opportunities within the development and financial inclusion sectors Why Apply? The Women’s World Banking internship program offers more than just professional experience. It provides an opportunity to contribute to global efforts aimed at improving women’s economic empowerment and financial security. Interns will gain valuable insight into: * Gender-focused financial inclusion strategies * International development practices * Public policy and advocacy processes * Research methodologies * Stakeholder engagement and partnership development * Global economic empowerment initiatives For students considering careers in international development, public policy, economics, finance, social impact, or nonprofit leadership, this internship can serve as a strong foundation for future professional growth. Eligibility Criteria Applicants should demonstrate: * Current enrollment in a graduate degree program * Strong interest in international development and women’s economic empowerment * Excellent research and analytical skills * Strong written and verbal communication abilities * Ability to work independently and collaboratively * Interest in financial inclusion and gender-focused development initiatives Specific qualifications may vary depending on the internship position. About the Women’s World Banking Institute The Women’s World Banking Institute serves as the organization’s research and learning arm. The Institute generates evidence-based insights and policy recommendations designed to improve women’s access to financial services and strengthen economic opportunities worldwide. Through rigorous research and policy engagement, the Institute helps shape discussions around women’s financial inclusion and contributes to solutions that drive sustainable economic growth. Application Process Interested candidates should review the internship descriptions carefully and submit their applications through the official Women’s World Banking careers portal. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since positions remain open until filled. Application Link Apply HERE Conclusion The Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 Internships provide graduate students with a unique opportunity to gain practical experience while contributing to one of the most important global development challenges—advancing women’s financial inclusion. Whether your interests lie in research, policy advocacy, economic development, or social impact, these internships offer meaningful work, professional growth, and the chance to support initiatives that improve the lives of women around the world. Interested candidates should submit their applications as soon as possible, as positions will remain open only until they are filled. title: American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 in Germany | Fully Funded Fellowship for Scholars, Journalists, Writers and Public Policy Professionals
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 , a fully funded international fellowship that brings outstanding scholars, writers, journalists, legal experts, and public policy professionals to Berlin for a semester-long residency. The American Academy in Berlin is one of the leading transatlantic institutions dedicated to strengthening intellectual and cultural ties between the United States and Germany. Each year, the Academy selects approximately 25 exceptional individuals through a highly competitive process and awards fellowships that allow recipients to pursue independent projects while engaging with Germany’s vibrant intellectual and cultural community. Fellows reside at the historic Hans Arnhold Center, located on the shores of Lake Wannsee in Berlin, where they become part of an interdisciplinary community of scholars and practitioners. In addition to receiving generous financial support, fellows participate in lectures, discussions, readings, and other public programs that contribute to transatlantic dialogue. The deadline for applications is September 25, 2026. About the American Academy in Berlin The American Academy in Berlin is an independent, nonprofit institute for advanced study that supports distinguished individuals working in: Arts Humanities Social Sciences Law Journalism Public Policy The institution s primary mission is to strengthen intellectual, academic, and cultural connections between the United States and Germany. Through its flagship Berlin Prize Fellowship, the Academy provides a unique opportunity for experts and thought leaders to advance their work in a stimulating international environment while building meaningful professional connections across disciplines. Fellowship Benefits Successful applicants will receive a comprehensive fellowship package that includes: Monthly Stipend Fellows receive a generous monthly stipend of **$5,000** throughout their residency. Roundtrip Airfare The Academy covers roundtrip travel expenses between the fellow s home location and Berlin. Accommodation Recipients are provided accommodation at or near the Academy s historic **Hans Arnhold Center** on Lake Wannsee. Partial Board The fellowship includes partial meal support during the residency period. Library and Research Resources Fellows receive access to the Academy s in-house library services and research support. Professional Networking Opportunities Participants become part of an influential network of academics, policymakers, journalists, writers, and public intellectuals. Public Engagement Opportunities Fellows present their work through: Public lectures Readings Panel discussions Film screenings Performances Academic events Fields and Disciplines Eligible for the Fellowship The Academy welcomes applications from individuals working in: Humanities Including history, philosophy, literature, religious studies, and related fields. Social Sciences Including sociology, political science, anthropology, economics, and related disciplines. Law Projects examining legal systems, public policy, governance, and justice. Journalism Investigative journalists, reporters, editors, and media professionals. Public Policy Professionals and researchers working on policy development and implementation. Specialized Fellowship Areas The Academy also offers dedicated support for projects in: Jewish Studies German Studies Public Health Biotechnology Priority Themes Although projects do not need to focus specifically on Germany, applicants are encouraged to explain how a residency in Berlin would enhance their work. The Academy particularly welcomes projects addressing pressing global issues such as: Democracy Security Technology and Society Artificial Intelligence (AI) Climate and Energy International Relations Global Order Public Health Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for individuals who demonstrate excellence in their respective fields. Eligible applicants include: Scholars Researchers Writers Journalists Legal Experts Public Policy Professionals Public Intellectuals Applicants should possess a strong record of professional achievement and a compelling project proposal. Who Cannot Apply? According to the Academy s guidelines: Visual artists must apply through separate nomination-based competitions. Composers are selected through separate nomination processes. Project proposals in mathematics and the natural sciences are generally not accepted. Residency Experience in Berlin Fellows live and work in Berlin while becoming part of an active intellectual community. The residency offers: Time and space for focused research and writing. Interaction with scholars and experts from different disciplines. Opportunities to engage with German institutions and organizations. Access to cultural and academic events. Participation in media and public engagement activities. The fellowship experience is designed to encourage meaningful exchange between American and German intellectual communities. Application Process Interested applicants should complete the online application before the deadline. Applicants should prepare all required application materials, including project information and supporting documentation as outlined in the official application portal. Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Why You Should Apply The Berlin Prize Fellowship is one of the most respected international fellowship programs available to scholars, journalists, writers, and policy professionals. The combination of financial support, accommodation, research time, public engagement opportunities, and access to Berlin s dynamic intellectual environment makes this an exceptional opportunity for professionals seeking to advance impactful projects. For those interested in contributing to international dialogue while benefiting from a world-class academic and cultural environment, the American Academy in Berlin Fellowship offers a transformative experience. Conclusion The American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 provides an outstanding opportunity for scholars, journalists, writers, legal experts, and public policy professionals to spend a semester in Germany pursuing meaningful projects while engaging with an influential international community. With a monthly stipend of $5,000, accommodation, airfare, networking opportunities, and access to exceptional intellectual resources, the fellowship offers the ideal environment for advancing innovative ideas and impactful work. Interested applicants should submit their applications before September 25, 2026. Discover more fellowship opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: UNICEF Youth Advisors 2026: Join the Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM)
summary: Applications are now open for the UNICEF Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) Youth Advisors 2026. UNICEF is seeking five young people aged 18–24 with lived experience of mental health and a passion for improving child and adolescent mental health (CAMH) data to join its global Technical Advisory Group for a two-year term . Youth advisors will work alongside leading researchers, practitioners, and technical experts to shape how UNICEF measures, tracks, and uses data on children s and adolescents mental health worldwide. Successful applicants will receive a USD 2,000 stipend over two years , travel support for in-person meetings, and opportunities to co-author technical outputs and participate in global advocacy initiatives. About the UNICEF TAG-CAMHM Youth Advisor Programme Mental health conditions are among the leading causes of illness and disability among adolescents globally. However, reliable and youth-informed data on child and adolescent mental health remains limited. To strengthen global mental health measurement, UNICEF is establishing the Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) —an independent body comprising researchers, practitioners, and youth advisors. As a Youth Advisor, you will serve as a full and equal member of the Technical Advisory Group, bringing your lived experiences and perspectives to influence how mental health data is collected, interpreted, and used. Key Summary Opportunity Details Organisation UNICEF Programme Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) – Youth Advisors Position Youth Advisor (5 positions available) Who Can Apply? Young people aged 18–24 with lived experience of mental health and engagement in child and adolescent mental health (CAMH)-related work Location Global (applications encouraged from all regions, especially the Global South) Duration Two-year advisory term (renewable) Stipend USD 1,000 per year (USD 2,000 over the two-year term) Benefits Equal membership on the Technical Advisory Group, fully funded travel for in-person meetings, mentorship, networking, opportunities to co-author publications, and participation in UNICEF initiatives Meetings Two per year (one virtual and one in-person/hybrid) Application Deadline 17 August 2026 How to Apply Submit a one-page statement of interest and a CV/resume (or approved alternative format) via email Application Email ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org Email Subject Youth Advisor Expression of Interest – TAG Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement Why This Matters Mental health conditions are among the leading causes of illness and disability among adolescents around the world. Yet the data and evidence that should be driving responses, including who is affected, how, and where, remain incomplete, inconsistently collected, and too rarely shaped by the perspectives of young people themselves. UNICEF is working to change that. UNICEF will convene a Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM), an independent group of researchers, practitioners, and youth advisors who will help shape how UNICEF measures, tracks, and uses data on children s and adolescents mental health. We are seeking five young people aged 18 to 24 to join the TAG as youth advisors. Youth advisors are full and equal members of the group. You would be contributing your lived experience and perspectives alongside senior researchers and technical experts, with equal standing in all discussions. What the Role Involves A. Advising on CAMH measurement As a full TAG member, you will: Attend and actively participate in TAG meetings twice a year. One meeting will be in person or hybrid and one will be virtual. Review documents and provide input on UNICEF s measurement tools and initiatives, including MMAPP, from the perspective of a young person with lived experience Share your views on what data young people need, how it should be collected, and how it should be used Contribute thought leadership on youth-focused and youth-led CAMH measurement: what data young people need, how it should be collected, and how it should be used Participate in working groups or ad hoc consultations as relevant B. Data and Research for Decision-Making workstream Youth advisors will also contribute to a related piece of UNICEF work focused on helping young people and governments use data and research more effectively in mental health decision-making. This workstream is developing two practical learning experiences: one designed for young people, and one designed for governments and implementing organisations. Both are built around real mental health data scenarios, and a third session brings both groups together to engage with each other around shared evidence. Your contribution to this work will involve: Co-designing the learning experience for young people, including the scenario content, facilitation approach, and associated guidance materials Contributing your perspective to the framework that guides how both tools are designed and used Providing input into related guidance and toolkit materials as they are developed C. Youth-identified activities Beyond these two areas, advisors are encouraged to propose additional contributions based on their own expertise and interests, such as co-authorship of technical papers, participation in advocacy forums, or engagement in related UNICEF initiatives. These are agreed with the Secretariat on an ongoing basis and form part of the overall engagement. Who We Are Looking For We are looking for five young people aged 18 to 24 at the time of recruitment, with lived experience of mental health and demonstrated engagement in CAMH-related work. You do not need to be a researcher or hold a formal academic qualification. What matters is your experience, your perspective, and your commitment to making sure that data and evidence on children s and adolescents mental health reflects and serves the communities most affected. You may be a strong candidate if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Advocating for better mental health policy, services, or systems at a national or international level Participating in or leading community-based or youth-led research or data collection on mental health Leading or playing an active role in a youth-led organisation focused on mental health, wellbeing, or children s rights Working to influence mental health policies, systems, or funding Using data or research to support mental health advocacy or to inform how programmes are designed UNICEF strongly encourages applications from young people based in or with substantial experience in the Global South, including Sub-Saharan Africa, South and South-East Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East and North Africa, and Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Diversity of background, thought, identity, and experience is essential to the work of the TAG. What UNICEF Offers Stipend USD 1,000 per year (USD 2,000 total over the two-year term), recognising the full scope of your engagement across TAG advisory activities, workstream co-design, and youth-identified contributions. Equal standing Youth advisors are full TAG members with equal voice in all deliberations — not observers or a separate youth panel. Your input carries the same weight as that of senior researchers and technical experts. Travel and support Travel and accommodation for in-person TAG meetings are covered by UNICEF for all youth members. You will receive tailored pre-meeting orientation, briefing materials in accessible language, and preparatory calls with the Secretariat as needed. Peer connections The Secretariat will facilitate connections between youth advisors and senior technical experts on the TAG, to support learning, mentorship, and collaboration. Recognition and opportunities TAG membership is a recognised advisory role that may be referenced on your CV and professional profiles. Advisors will have opportunities to co-author technical outputs, attend and speak at relevant events, and engage in related UNICEF initiatives as part of the role. Conditions of Appointment Youth advisors serve a two-year term, with the possibility of renewal All advisors serve in their individual capacity and do not represent any government, organisation, or institution Members are required to complete a Declaration of Interests before appointment and to maintain confidentiality regarding TAG discussions The working language of the TAG is English Stipend payments are linked to active participation. Advisors are expected to engage meaningfully across the full scope of the role. How to Apply To express interest in serving as a TAG youth advisor, please submit the following to ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org by August 17 , using the subject line Youth Advisor Expression of Interest – TAG Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement : A short statement (maximum one page) describing your interest in the role, what you would bring to the TAG, and any relevant experience in CAMH advocacy, research, or evidence use. Write in whatever way feels natural to you. Please include a note of any conflicts of interest relevant to your participation. A brief CV/resume or professional profile (maximum two pages), including relevant experience, initiatives you have been involved in, or organisations you are part of We recognise that not everyone has a traditional CV/resume. If you would prefer to share your experience in a different format, for example a portfolio, a short video, or a written description of your work, please contact us before the deadline to discuss alternatives. Due to the expected volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. UNICEF may hold conversations with shortlisted candidates as part of the selection process. Selection is at UNICEF s sole discretion, taking into account lived experience, engagement in CAMH-related work, geographic and identity diversity, and communication skills. For questions, please write to ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org well before the deadline. title: DAFI Scholarship Programme 2026/2027 in Rwanda: Fully Funded Undergraduate Scholarships for Refugees and Asylum Seekers
summary: Applications Deadline: 7 August 2026 Are you a refugee or asylum seeker in Rwanda looking to pursue a university education? Applications are now open for the UNHCR Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative (DAFI) Scholarship Programme for the 2026/2027 academic year . The DAFI Scholarship is a fully funded higher education programme that enables qualified refugee and returnee students to earn an undergraduate degree or accredited technical qualification in their country of asylum or home country. Since its inception, the programme has transformed the lives of thousands of refugee students worldwide, including more than 600 scholars in Rwanda . If you meet the eligibility requirements, this is your opportunity to access quality higher education while developing leadership, professional, and community engagement skills. About the UNHCR DAFI Scholarship Programme The DAFI (Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative) Scholarship Programme is managed by UNHCR and supports refugee students in pursuing undergraduate (Bachelor s) degrees and selected Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes. The scholarship supports programmes classified under: ISCED Level 6: Bachelor s degrees or equivalent qualifications ISCED Level 5: Accredited TVET programmes lasting two years or more, leading to a diploma or certification Beyond financial assistance, DAFI scholars receive continuous academic support, mentorship, and opportunities to participate in leadership, skills development, and community engagement activities throughout their studies. Please note: The DAFI Scholarship does not fund Master s degree programmes. DAFI Scholarship Benefits The scholarship package varies depending on the country but generally covers: Full tuition fees Study materials and learning resources Food allowance Transportation costs Accommodation support Academic monitoring and student support Leadership and community engagement opportunities DAFI Scholarship Eligibility Criteria (Rwanda) To be eligible, applicants must: Be a recognized refugee or asylum seeker living in Rwanda Demonstrate strong academic performance (priority is given to outstanding students) Have been admitted to a university in Rwanda and provide proof of admission Not currently be receiving another higher education scholarship Not have been approved for resettlement to a third country Ensure that only one member per family applies or receives the DAFI Scholarship Additional Selection Considerations UNHCR particularly encourages applications from: Female applicants Persons with disabilities or special educational needs Required Documents Applicants must upload the following documents: UNHCR Proof of Registration Official or certified copy of high school diploma University admission letter or proof of acceptance from a university in Rwanda Equivalence certificate issued by the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum Ensure that all documents are complete before submitting your application. How to Apply for the DAFI Scholarship 2026/2027 Eligible applicants must complete the online DAFI application form and upload all required supporting documents before the application deadline. All application should be submitted through DAFI online application form, available at the following link: Rwanda 2026 DAFI Call for applications Application Deadline Opening Date: 15 July 2026 Closing Date: 7 August 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Need Application Support? Applicants experiencing internet connectivity challenges or difficulties uploading documents can seek assistance from: The nearest Digital Career Counsellor in their refugee camp A nearby Community Centre For any inquiries, please contact us via rwakibarizahano@unhcr.org and aurea_kagwesage@wvi.org Final Thoughts The UNHCR DAFI Scholarship Programme 2026/2027 provides refugee and asylum-seeking students in Rwanda with an invaluable opportunity to obtain a fully funded undergraduate education while building the knowledge, leadership, and professional skills needed for future success. If you meet the eligibility criteria, be sure to submit your application before 7 August 2026 . All application should be submitted through DAFI online application form, available at the following link: Rwanda 2026 DAFI Call for applications For more scholarships and educational opportunities, keep visiting Opportunities For Youth. title: Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarships 2026/2027 in Germany for International Master’s and PhD Students
summary: Germany continues to be one of the world s most attractive destinations for higher education, offering internationally recognized universities, world-class research institutions, and numerous funding opportunities for outstanding students from around the globe. One of the most prestigious opportunities currently open is the Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship Program, designed specifically to support talented international graduate students and doctoral candidates from developing countries who wish to study in Germany. The Heinrich Böll Foundation is committed to promoting equal opportunities, educational access, academic excellence, sustainability, democracy, human rights, and social responsibility. Through this scholarship program, the foundation seeks to empower future leaders who demonstrate exceptional academic potential, social engagement, and a commitment to creating positive change within their communities and beyond. Whether you are planning to pursue a Master s degree or embark on a PhD journey in Germany, this scholarship can significantly reduce your financial burden while providing access to a vibrant international academic community and numerous professional development opportunities. About the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship The Tailwind for Talents Scholarship is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA). It is specifically designed to provide financial and academic support to international students from eligible developing countries who aspire to continue their education in Germany. Beyond financial assistance, scholarship recipients become part of a dynamic network of scholars, researchers, professionals, and alumni who are actively engaged in shaping a more democratic, environmentally sustainable, and socially just world. The scholarship combines financial funding with extensive academic support, networking opportunities, leadership development, and participation in educational events organized by the Heinrich Böll Foundation. Why Choose the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship? The scholarship is more than financial support—it is an investment in future global leaders. Successful applicants benefit from: Financial support throughout their studies. Funding supported by the German government. Opportunities to study at leading German universities. Access to academic mentoring and professional guidance. Participation in seminars, workshops, conferences, and networking events. Leadership development opportunities. Membership in an international community of scholars. Access to an extensive alumni network. Opportunities for interdisciplinary learning. Exposure to Germany s academic, research, and innovation ecosystem. Support services that help students successfully settle into academic life in Germany. Who Can Apply? The scholarship welcomes applications from outstanding international students who meet the eligibility requirements. For Master s Students Applicants must: Have completed their first university degree outside Germany. Intend to begin a Master s degree at a university in Germany. Submit their application before commencing their Master s studies in Germany. Demonstrate academic excellence and motivation. The foundation gives priority consideration to applicants from OECD DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time they apply. For PhD Applicants Applicants must: Have completed a graduate degree outside Germany. Intend to pursue a PhD at a recognized German institution. Meet the academic requirements for doctoral study in Germany. Demonstrate strong research potential and commitment to societal impact. Priority is also given to applicants from OECD DAC countries who have not yet established residence in Germany. Scholarship Benefits Although individual funding may vary depending on the applicant s academic level and circumstances, recipients receive comprehensive support that may include: Financial assistance to support living expenses. Academic support throughout the duration of study. Participation in educational seminars. Professional development activities. Leadership and civic engagement training. Networking with scholars from around the world. Access to the Heinrich Böll Foundation s extensive alumni community. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. Ongoing mentoring and institutional support. Academic Support Beyond Funding One distinguishing feature of the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship is its holistic approach to supporting scholars. Recipients benefit from various non-financial opportunities, including: Academic Development Research support. Academic mentoring. Workshops and seminars. Educational events. Professional Development Leadership training. Communication skills development. Networking opportunities. Career guidance. Community Engagement The foundation encourages scholars to actively contribute to society by participating in: Social initiatives. Environmental sustainability projects. Democratic engagement. Human rights advocacy. Civic participation. Application Process Applicants should carefully review all official application documents before submitting their applications. Separate application guides are available for: Master s degree applicants. PhD applicants. These guides contain detailed eligibility requirements, required documents, application procedures, and submission instructions. Prospective applicants are also encouraged to review the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ), which provides clarification on the selection process and online application procedures. Important Application Deadlines Applicants should note the following application periods: Fall 2026 Intake Application Opens: 15 July 2026 Application Deadline: 1 September 2026 Spring 2027 Intake Application Opens: 15 January 2027 Application Deadline: 1 March 2027 Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their documents well in advance to avoid last-minute submission challenges. Required Preparation Before Applying Before beginning your application, it is advisable to: Confirm your eligibility. Review the official application information sheet. Gather all required supporting documents. Prepare any required academic statements. Ensure your academic qualifications meet German university admission requirements. Read the Frequently Asked Questions. Submit your application before the relevant deadline. Why Study in Germany? Germany has become one of the world s leading destinations for international higher education due to: High-quality universities. Strong research infrastructure. Internationally recognized degrees. Excellent career opportunities. Diverse academic community. Affordable education compared to many other study destinations. Strong links between academia and industry. Rich cultural experiences. Receiving a Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship further enhances this experience by providing financial stability and access to an influential network of scholars and professionals. Contact Information Applicants seeking additional information may contact: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship Department Schumannstraße 8 10117 Berlin, Germany Telephone: +49 (0) 30 285 34-400 Fax: +49 (0) 30 285 34-409 Email: studienwerk@boell.de Office Hours: Monday Tuesday Thursday Friday 10:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. (Germany Time) For more information about this scholarship, visit the Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship HERE For more scholarships opportunities visit OFY Website HERE Conclusion The Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship represents an outstanding opportunity for ambitious international students from eligible developing countries who aspire to pursue advanced studies in Germany. By combining generous financial assistance with leadership development, academic mentoring, professional networking, and community engagement, the scholarship empowers scholars to excel academically while preparing them to become influential leaders in their respective fields. If you meet the eligibility requirements and are passionate about academic excellence, social responsibility, and making a meaningful impact in your community, this scholarship offers an excellent pathway to achieving your educational and professional goals. Interested applicants should begin preparing their application materials early and submit their applications before the applicable deadline to maximize their chances of success. title: OHCHR Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027: Fully Funded UN Human Rights Fellowship in Geneva
summary: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is now accepting applications for the Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 . This prestigious, fully funded fellowship offers indigenous leaders from around the world an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge of the United Nations human rights system and gain practical skills to advance and protect the rights of indigenous peoples. The programme brings together fellows from different regions and language backgrounds for an intensive four-week training in Geneva, Switzerland , while providing a unique opportunity to engage directly with UN human rights mechanisms. Key Summary Host: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) Programme: Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 Location: Geneva, Switzerland Duration: 4 weeks (June/July 2027) Funding: Fully funded (return airfare, living expenses, and basic health insurance) Languages: English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese Eligibility: Indigenous persons nominated by an indigenous organization or community Education Requirement: No formal educational qualifications required Application Deadline: 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) Application Method: Online application with a recommendation letter from the nominating indigenous organization or community General information: The Indigenous Fellowship Programme was launched in 1997 by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in the context of the first International Decade of the World s Indigenous People. The aim of the programme is to give indigenous persons the opportunity to gain knowledge about the UN system and mechanisms dealing with human rights issues in general and indigenous issues in particular. Trained participants are better equipped to assist their organisations and communities in protecting and promoting their rights. This training programme is available in 4 languages: English , Spanish , French and Portuguese . When does it take place? Fellows from all 4 language components of the programme are trained together with simultaneous interpretation over 4 weeks in Geneva . The date of the training programme usually coincides with the annual session of the Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples ( June/July each year), allowing the fellows to participate more actively in that Mechanism. What does the programme cover? The selected candidates are entitled to a return flight ticket, living expenses and basic health insurance for the duration of the training. Who can apply for the programme? The candidate must be indigenous (non-indigenous persons will not be taken into consideration, even if they have close links with indigenous communities and/or organizations). Indigenous candidates, including women, LGBTQI+ individuals, and persons with disabilities, are strongly encouraged to apply. Age should not be a limitation to participation in the programme. Formal education should not be a limitation to participation in the IFP given the socio-economic barriers confronted by many indigenous peoples that limit access to formal educational institutions. Candidates should agree to train other indigenous persons after the return to their respective communities/organizations. The candidate should be proposed, and his/her candidacy supported by his/her indigenous organization and/or community. It is desirable that the sponsoring organization has a firm constituency or membership and that it is representative. The candidate should have a good working knowledge of the language in which the programme is imparted. Application procedure: We strongly encourage you to submit you online application well before the deadline of 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) . Fellowship applications will only be taken into consideration if they are fully completed. Both parts I and II of the application form must be completed Application forms must include an official recommendation letter from the nominating Indigenous organization or community. Applicants should upload their recommendation letters directly to the online application form. The application form is available at: https://survey.ohchr.org/429282?lang=en Selection process: The selection of fellows reflects a gender and regional balance, as well as a balance between communities represented. The general human rights situation in the respective regions/countries is also taken into consideration. A pre-selection of 15 to 20 candidates per language group is made by previous indigenous fellows. The selection process also entails interviews of pre-selected candidates who applied to either the English, French, Spanish or Portuguese language components of the programme. The final selection of successful candidates is reviewed by an advisory group composed of OHCHR staff. In view of the large number of applications, ONLY PRE-SELECTED CANDIDATES ARE CONTACTED. Any other questions? Any question pertaining to the Indigenous Fellowship Programme can be e-mailed to: ohchr-fellowship@un.org . title: Ghana2Germany Initiative Opens Applications for Lifeguard Training and Germany Apprenticeship Pathway for Young Ghanaians
summary: Young Ghanaians seeking to build internationally recognized skills while preparing for future apprenticeship opportunities in Germany now have an exciting opportunity through the ghana2germany initiative . Implemented by the Delegation of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana (AHK Ghana) in collaboration with GIZ Ghana through the Ghanaian European Centre for Migration (GEC) , the initiative is designed to strengthen technical and vocational skills, improve employability, and create pathways to international careers. As part of this initiative, the programme has partnered with the Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association (GHALDA) to provide specialized training in swimming, lifesaving, and water safety for young people in Kumasi. Successful applicants will receive comprehensive professional training leading to nationally and internationally recognized lifeguard certifications, German language instruction, and the opportunity to pursue dual apprenticeship training in Germany. The programme represents an important investment in youth development by combining technical skills, language training, and international career preparation into one structured pathway. About the Ghana2Germany Initiative The ghana2germany initiative is a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) support programme established to improve the quality of vocational education while preparing young people for employment opportunities in Ghana and Germany. The programme focuses on strengthening technical competencies, improving soft skills, and enhancing vocational training institutions so that graduates possess industry-relevant knowledge and practical experience. Beyond improving training institutions, the initiative seeks to create a highly skilled workforce capable of meeting labour market demands in both Ghana and Germany through internationally aligned vocational education and apprenticeship opportunities. Partnership Behind the Programme The programme is implemented through collaboration among several organizations committed to youth development and international vocational training. These include: Delegation of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana (AHK Ghana) GIZ Ghana Ghanaian European Centre for Migration (GEC) Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association (GHALDA) Together, these organizations combine expertise in vocational education, migration support, technical skills development, and international cooperation to deliver a comprehensive training programme. Purpose of the Programme The ghana2germany initiative aims to prepare young Ghanaians for meaningful employment by providing practical vocational education that aligns with current industry needs. Its objectives include: Strengthening technical skills. Developing soft skills required in modern workplaces. Improving TVET workshop facilities. Enhancing vocational education quality. Building industry-relevant competencies. Preparing participants for dual apprenticeship opportunities. Supporting labour mobility between Ghana and Germany. Creating a highly qualified workforce. Expanding international employment opportunities. Promoting safe swimming and lifesaving practices. Specialized Lifeguard Training Programme As part of this initiative, a dedicated lifeguard training programme has been introduced in partnership with GHALDA. The programme aims to provide participants with advanced practical training in: Swimming Lifesaving Water rescue Water safety Emergency response Participants will develop professional competencies required for lifeguard responsibilities while meeting recognized certification standards. Number of Participants The programme will pre-select fifteen (15) young Ghanaians to participate in the comprehensive training programme. Only shortlisted candidates will progress through the selection process following evaluation against the programme s internal eligibility criteria. Training Components Successful participants will receive extensive professional development covering multiple areas. 1. Professional Swimming Training Participants will improve their swimming skills through structured instruction designed to prepare them for professional lifesaving responsibilities. Training may include: Swimming techniques Endurance development Water confidence Rescue swimming Practical assessments 2. Lifesaving Skills Training Participants will receive specialized instruction in professional lifesaving techniques. Areas of focus include: Rescue procedures Emergency response Victim assistance Water rescue operations Public safety 3. Water Safety Education Understanding water safety is an essential part of professional lifeguarding. Training includes: Risk identification Accident prevention Public awareness Safe swimming practices Hazard management 4. National Lifeguard Certification Participants who successfully complete the programme will work toward obtaining a National Lifeguard Certification/License , demonstrating their competence according to national standards. 5. International Lifeguard License Beyond national certification, trainees will also have the opportunity to earn an International Lifeguard License , enhancing their professional credentials and improving employability internationally. 6. German Language Training Language preparation forms an important component of the programme. Selected participants will receive German language instruction covering: A1 Level A2 Level Developing language skills prepares participants for future apprenticeship and work opportunities in Germany. Opportunity for Dual Apprenticeship Training in Germany One of the programme s most significant features is the opportunity for selected participants to travel to Germany for dual apprenticeship training . Germany s dual apprenticeship model combines classroom instruction with practical workplace experience, allowing participants to build technical expertise while gaining hands-on industry experience. Participation in this pathway may significantly improve future employment prospects. However, applicants should note that submission of an application does not guarantee placement, employment, sponsorship, or relocation. Long-Term Career Prospects The initiative seeks to prepare participants for future opportunities by equipping them with internationally relevant skills. Potential long-term outcomes include: Improved employability International vocational experience Professional certification Enhanced technical competencies Language proficiency Greater competitiveness in the labour market Access to apprenticeship opportunities in Germany Application Process Interested applicants are required to complete the official application form carefully and provide accurate information throughout the process. Applicants are advised to: Complete every section carefully. Provide truthful information. Ensure all personal details are accurate. Submit complete responses. Incomplete or misleading information may negatively affect the application. Information Required During Application Applicants will be asked to provide information including: Personal Information Full name Date of birth Nationality Gender City or region of residence Residential address Phone number Email address Educational Background Applicants must indicate: Highest educational qualification obtained Name of educational institution Educational options include: JHS SHS TVET Institution Diploma Degree Swimming Experience Applicants will provide information regarding: Ability to swim without assistance Swimming proficiency level Previous formal swimming training Swimming ability categories include: Beginner Intermediate Advanced Competitive Swimmer Previous Training Applicants may indicate previous participation in: Lifeguard Training Swimming Instructor Training Water Safety Programmes Diving Training Rescue Swimming Training Applicants with no previous experience may also apply. Professional Certifications Applicants will indicate whether they currently hold certifications related to: Swimming Lifesaving First Aid CPR Emergency Response If applicable, applicants should provide details. Motivation Questions Applicants are also required to answer written questions covering: Why they wish to become certified lifeguards. Personal qualities that make them suitable for the programme. Examples demonstrating leadership, responsibility, or emergency response. These responses help assess motivation and suitability beyond technical qualifications. Selection Process Submitting an application does not guarantee : Selection Participation Employment Sponsorship Placement Apprenticeship Visa support Future work opportunities Applications will be evaluated according to internally established eligibility criteria. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Selected candidates can expect an email invitation for interviews approximately one week after submitting their application. Applicant Declaration Applicants must confirm that: Information provided is accurate. False information may result in disqualification. Participation in selection does not guarantee programme admission. They understand certification and employment are not guaranteed. Applicants must also provide their signature by entering their full name in capital letters. Health and Participation Requirements Applicants confirm that they: Are physically fit for intensive swimming and rescue training. Do not have medical conditions affecting participation. Are willing to learn German. Are willing to relocate to Germany if future apprenticeship or employment opportunities become available. These declarations ensure participants are prepared for the demands of the programme. Important Disclaimer The programme emphasizes that applicants who are not contacted should consider their application unsuccessful for the current intake. However, unsuccessful applicants are encouraged to remain optimistic, as future opportunities under the ghana2germany initiative may become available. Visit here for more details on Ghana2Germany Initiative Opens Applications for Lifeguard Training and Germany Apprenticeship Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified in the available information. Interested applicants are encouraged to complete and submit their application as early as possible before the selection process advances. Apply here Why This Programme Stands Out The ghana2germany initiative offers far more than technical training. By combining internationally recognized lifeguard certification, German language education, vocational development, and the possibility of participating in Germany s dual apprenticeship system, the programme creates a unique pathway for young Ghanaians to develop valuable skills and broaden their career prospects. Its integrated approach supports both personal and professional development while strengthening the connection between vocational education in Ghana and international labour market opportunities. Conclusion The ghana2germany initiative represents a significant opportunity for young Ghanaians interested in developing professional skills in swimming, lifesaving, and water safety while preparing for potential apprenticeship opportunities in Germany. Through collaboration between AHK Ghana, GIZ Ghana, the Ghanaian European Centre for Migration, and the Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association, the programme delivers high-quality vocational training, internationally recognized certifications, German language instruction, and exposure to Germany s dual apprenticeship model. Although selection is competitive and participation does not guarantee employment or relocation, the initiative provides participants with valuable technical competencies, leadership experience, and internationally relevant qualifications that can strengthen their long-term career prospects. Eligible young Ghanaians who are motivated, physically fit, and committed to professional development are encouraged to submit a complete and accurate application for this unique training opportunity. title: GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025: Empowering the Next Generation of Global Climate Leaders for a Carbon-Neutral Future
summary: Climate change remains one of the defining challenges of the 21st century, affecting economies, ecosystems, communities, and future generations across the globe. As countries accelerate efforts to achieve carbon neutrality and sustainable development, there is an increasing need for young leaders equipped with the knowledge, leadership skills, and interdisciplinary understanding required to drive meaningful climate action. Recognizing this urgent need, the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) has launched the 2025 Climate x Leadership Training Program , an international learning initiative designed to prepare young people to become leaders in the global transition toward a carbon-neutral future. The program seeks to empower youth by providing them with comprehensive knowledge, practical tools, and leadership capabilities that enable them to understand climate challenges, explore innovative solutions, and contribute to sustainable development at local, national, and international levels. Built around the concept of interdisciplinary climate leadership, the Climate x Leadership Training Program encourages participants to look beyond traditional environmental approaches and understand how climate action connects with every aspect of sustainable development. About the Climate x Leadership Training Program The Climate x Leadership Training Program is an educational initiative developed by the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) to prepare future leaders capable of addressing the complex challenges posed by climate change. Rather than focusing solely on environmental science, the program adopts a multidisciplinary perspective, recognizing that climate change intersects with economics, governance, agriculture, food systems, resilience, public policy, innovation, and sustainable development. Participants are introduced to the knowledge, perspectives, and leadership competencies needed to contribute effectively to global climate solutions while understanding the interconnected nature of today s development challenges. The program emphasizes that achieving carbon neutrality requires a comprehensive transformation of societies, economies, and institutions rather than simply replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy sources. Program Vision The Climate x Leadership Training Program is built around the vision of creating a new generation of globally minded climate leaders who can support the transition toward sustainable and carbon-neutral development. According to GAUC, transitioning to a carbon-neutral economy represents far more than an energy transition. It involves: Transforming economic systems Rethinking development models Promoting sustainable modernization Protecting natural ecosystems Encouraging innovation Supporting inclusive economic growth Building resilient societies Creating a greener and more prosperous future Through this program, participants are encouraged to understand climate action within this broader global context. Program Objectives The Climate x Leadership Training Program seeks to achieve several important objectives. These include: Empowering youth with climate knowledge Developing future climate leaders Building interdisciplinary understanding Promoting sustainable development Encouraging innovation Supporting carbon neutrality goals Strengthening leadership capacity Inspiring meaningful climate action Equipping participants with practical tools Developing global perspectives on sustainability Ultimately, the program aims to prepare participants to become active contributors to climate solutions within their communities, institutions, and countries. Why the Climate x Initiative Matters Climate challenges cannot be solved through isolated actions. The Climate x initiative emphasizes that today s global issues are deeply interconnected. Environmental sustainability is linked with: Economic development Food security Public health Education Social inclusion Governance Innovation Infrastructure Energy systems Global cooperation By recognizing these relationships, the program encourages participants to develop integrated solutions capable of generating positive outcomes across multiple sectors. Climate Action and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) One of the central ideas behind the Climate x Leadership Training Program is that climate action should be pursued alongside the broader United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) . Rather than treating climate change as a separate issue, the program encourages participants to understand how climate solutions contribute to progress across the remaining SDGs. This integrated approach supports: Sustainable economic growth Poverty reduction Food security Environmental protection Clean energy Responsible consumption Innovation Strong institutions Global partnerships The program highlights the importance of creating synergies between climate action and sustainable development. A Vision from Global Climate Leadership The Climate x Leadership Training Program features insights from Lord Nicholas Stern , Chair of GAUC s Academic Committee and Chair of the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) . The initiative reflects the belief that young people are not merely inheritors of the future but also its creators, owners, and leaders. The program emphasizes that empowering youth with the right knowledge and leadership skills is essential for achieving a successful transition to a net-zero future. Program Structure The Climate x Leadership Training Program includes an intensive one-month knowledge immersion experience designed to provide participants with both foundational understanding and practical perspectives on climate leadership. During the program, learners engage with key themes that shape global climate action and sustainable development. Learning Areas The curriculum is organized around several important subject areas. 1. Climate x Adaptation Resilience Participants explore strategies for helping societies adapt to climate change while strengthening resilience against environmental, economic, and social risks. Topics may include: Climate adaptation Disaster resilience Community resilience Risk reduction Sustainable planning Long-term climate preparedness 2. Climate x Food Food systems play a critical role in both contributing to and addressing climate change. This module introduces participants to issues such as: Sustainable agriculture Food security Climate-smart farming Environmental sustainability Agricultural innovation Resilient food systems 3. Global Climate Governance Climate action depends upon cooperation among governments, international organizations, institutions, businesses, and communities. Participants gain insight into: International climate agreements Global cooperation Climate diplomacy Climate policy International institutions Governance frameworks 4. Youth Leadership Developing leadership capacity is a central focus of the program. Participants strengthen skills including: Leadership Communication Collaboration Strategic thinking Problem-solving Global citizenship Change management Innovation Why Youth Are Central to the Program GAUC recognizes young people as essential partners in building a carbon-neutral future. The program highlights that youth are: Future leaders Current innovators Decision-makers of tomorrow Contributors to sustainable development Drivers of climate action Agents of positive change By investing in youth leadership today, the program aims to support long-term global sustainability. Benefits of Participating Although the available information does not list formal participant benefits, learners can expect opportunities to: Build knowledge of climate change and sustainability Strengthen leadership skills Understand carbon neutrality Explore interdisciplinary climate solutions Learn from an internationally focused curriculum Develop a broader understanding of global climate governance Enhance professional and academic knowledge Join a community interested in climate leadership Visit here for more details on GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025 About the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) The Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) is an international network dedicated to advancing climate education, research, collaboration, and leadership. Through educational initiatives such as the Climate x Leadership Training Program, GAUC seeks to mobilize universities, researchers, students, and young professionals to contribute toward global climate solutions and sustainable development. The alliance promotes interdisciplinary learning and international cooperation to help prepare future leaders capable of addressing complex environmental challenges. Registration and Updates Individuals interested in the Climate x Leadership Training Program can register their interest through the official GAUC platform. Prospective participants may choose to: Receive reminders when admissions begin. Subscribe to the GAUC Newsletter for updates on future programs, climate education initiatives, and related opportunities. Apply here Application Deadline No application deadline has been announced in the available information. Interested participants are encouraged to register their interest through the official GAUC website and subscribe for admission notifications. Why This Program Is Worth Considering The Climate x Leadership Training Program offers an opportunity for young people to build a strong foundation in climate leadership while exploring how climate action intersects with global development. Its interdisciplinary approach encourages participants to think beyond traditional environmental solutions and develop a broader understanding of sustainability, governance, innovation, and resilience. As governments, businesses, and organizations increasingly prioritize climate action and carbon neutrality, individuals with knowledge of climate leadership and sustainable development will be well positioned to contribute meaningfully across a wide range of sectors. Conclusion The GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025 is an important global initiative designed to prepare young leaders for the challenges and opportunities of a carbon-neutral future. By combining interdisciplinary learning with leadership development, the program equips participants to understand the complex relationships between climate change, sustainable development, governance, resilience, and innovation. Open to youth worldwide, the one-month knowledge immersion experience encourages participants to become active contributors to global climate solutions while developing the skills needed to lead positive environmental and societal change. For students, emerging professionals, and aspiring climate leaders seeking to expand their understanding of sustainability and leadership, the Climate x Leadership Training Program offers a valuable opportunity to engage with one of the most significant global issues of our time. title: UNDP & ISS Call for Papers 2026: Submit Your Research on Youth-Safe Digital Futures in Africa
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) , in partnership with the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) , has officially launched the Call for Papers: Youth-Safe Digital Futures , inviting researchers, practitioners, youth experts, digital rights advocates, and technology policy specialists from across Africa to contribute to an important new policy compendium focused on creating safer, more inclusive digital environments for young people. The forthcoming publication, titled Youth-Safe Digital Futures: From Digital Inclusion to Responsible AI for Peace and Development in Africa, seeks high-quality analytical papers that explore how Africa can build digital ecosystems where young people can safely access opportunities, participate in governance, innovate, and benefit from emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI). As digital transformation accelerates across Africa, this initiative recognizes that providing internet access alone is no longer enough. Instead, the focus is shifting toward ensuring that digital technologies promote peace, inclusion, accountability, innovation, and sustainable development while protecting young people from online risks and harms. Researchers and practitioners with expertise in digital governance, AI, youth development, peacebuilding, cybersecurity, media, and public policy are encouraged to submit original policy papers before the application deadline. About the Youth-Safe Digital Futures Compendium Young Africans are increasingly using digital platforms to: Access education. Build sustainable livelihoods. Launch startups and social enterprises. Participate in civic engagement. Advocate for policy change. Contribute to democratic processes. Engage in entrepreneurship and innovation. However, rapid digital transformation has also introduced numerous challenges. Young people frequently encounter: Online harassment. Cyber scams and fraud. Surveillance. Algorithmic discrimination. Digital exclusion. Online misinformation and disinformation. Manipulated digital content. Technology-facilitated violence. Limited representation of African languages and local realities in AI systems. Recognizing these challenges, the UNDP and ISS are developing a policy compendium that moves beyond digital access toward creating youth-safe digital futures , where young people can participate confidently, safely, and meaningfully in digital and AI-enabled societies. Purpose of the Compendium The publication seeks to answer several critical policy questions, including: How can African youth access and benefit from AI-enabled transformation? What governance mechanisms are needed to minimize AI-related risks? How can digital trust be strengthened to promote peace and social cohesion? How can AI contribute positively to sustainable development? Who benefits from AI-driven innovation? How can digital systems become more inclusive, equitable, and accountable? The publication aligns with major regional and global policy frameworks, including: African Union Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa (2020–2030) African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy Global Digital Compact UNDP Digital and Artificial Intelligence Strategy Scope of the Publication The compendium will include: 8–10 thematic policy papers 3–4 African case studies A comprehensive synthesis chapter outlining a policy agenda for youth-safe digital futures across Africa Contributors are expected to provide analytical and evidence-based papers rather than descriptive summaries. Papers should connect local experiences with national, regional, and continental policy discussions while drawing primarily on African evidence and experiences. Thematic Areas Authors should submit papers addressing one of the following four themes. Theme 1: Digital and AI Inclusion for Peace and Development Topics may include: Digital inclusion Affordable internet access AI literacy Digital literacy Rural and urban digital inequalities Gender gaps in digital access Disability inclusion Local language technologies Online safety Algorithmic bias Digital exclusion Theme 2: Safe Digital Spaces, Rights and Protection Possible topics include: Cyberbullying Online harassment Technology-facilitated gender-based violence Digital scams Online exploitation Extremist recruitment Privacy and surveillance Mental health and digital wellbeing Digital rights Child and youth online protection Theme 3: Information Integrity, Media and Social Cohesion Authors may explore: Misinformation Disinformation Hate speech Election-related misinformation Digital trust Social media governance Civic participation Fact-checking Digital media Peacebuilding through information integrity Theme 4: Youth Innovation, Digital Livelihoods and Resilience Suggested areas include: Artificial Intelligence innovation Youth entrepreneurship Digital startups Creative industries Climate technology Civic technology Community resilience Peacebuilding innovation Financing digital innovation Public-private partnerships Who Should Submit Papers? The organizers welcome submissions from individuals and organizations with expertise in relevant fields. Eligible contributors include: Researchers Academics Youth experts Civil society organizations Technology policy specialists Digital rights advocates Peacebuilding practitioners Think tanks Development professionals Youth-led organizations Editorial Requirements Submitted papers must: Be approximately 2,000 words . Present original analysis. Be intellectually authored by humans. Not be simultaneously submitted elsewhere. Successfully pass plagiarism screening. Undergo editorial review. Undergo external peer review. While AI-assisted tools may be used for editing, transcription, coding, translation, or literature organization, authors must disclose such use. AI-generated papers will not be accepted. Required Paper Structure Each submission should include: Executive summary or abstract. Problem statement. Definitions of key concepts. Methodology section. Evidence-based analysis. Gender considerations. Youth inclusion considerations. Disability inclusion considerations. Conflict-sensitive analysis. Policy recommendations at: Community level National level Regional level Continental level Complete reference list using: APA 7th Edition, or Chicago Author-Date referencing style Submission Process Authors should submit their completed 2,000-word paper by email. Submissions should be sent to: Raquel Leandro – raquel.leandro@undp.org Christella Igiraneza – christella.igiraneza@undp.org Emmaculate Liaga – eliaga@issafrica.org Important Dates Activity Date Call for Papers Opens 23 July 2026 Submission Deadline 31 August 2026 Internal Review End of September 2026 External Peer Review Mid-October 2026 Editing and Finalization Mid-November – December 2026 For More Information To learn more about the Youth-Safe Digital Futures Call for Papers , including submission requirements, thematic guidance, editorial expectations, and the complete announcement, applicants should visit the official UNDP Africa webpage HERE Prospective contributors are encouraged to review the official guidance carefully before preparing and submitting their papers to ensure they meet all editorial and submission requirements. Why You Should Apply This Call for Papers provides a valuable opportunity to contribute to one of Africa s most important policy discussions on digital transformation, artificial intelligence, youth participation, and peacebuilding. Selected contributors will help shape evidence-based recommendations that can influence digital governance, AI policy, and youth-focused development across the continent. Whether you are a researcher, policymaker, practitioner, or digital rights advocate, your work can contribute to building a future where Africa s young people not only access digital technologies but also use them safely, equitably, and meaningfully. Conclusion The UNDP and ISS Youth-Safe Digital Futures Call for Papers 2026 offers an important platform for African experts to contribute original research and policy analysis on the future of digital inclusion, AI governance, online safety, and youth empowerment. By bringing together evidence from across the continent, this compendium aims to inform policies that strengthen peace, digital rights, innovation, and inclusive development. Interested contributors should begin preparing their original analytical papers early and submit them no later than 31 August 2026 to be considered for inclusion in this landmark publication.
